post.description:
Creates an identity provider based on a configuration in the JSON format. When you create an identity provider, certain limitations apply depending on what protocol you use.

- **OpenID Connect**
A subaccount can only have one custom OIDC identity provider. Additionally, a subaccount may also have exactly one default OIDC identity provider. When creating a custom OIDC identity provider, a limited list of Identity Authentication tenants can be chosen. The Identity Authentication tenant must be assigned to the same customer ID and your global account. At a minimum, include iasTenant of the Identity Authentication tenant and type oidc1.0. To see which tenants are available for your account, use the GET method to call the /sap/rest/identity-providers/ias endpoint.
- **SAML**
No limitations apply, though we recommend you configure an OIDC configuration for your Identity Authentication tenant. To add a SAML configuration, you can include type, name, origin key, SAML metadata configuration, alias for your identity provider, SAML link, attribute mappings, addition of shadow users on login, and whether the identity provider is active.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: Configuration of the identity provider in JSON format.

parameters.name: rawConfig
parameters.description: If this parameter is set to true, the return value is of the type object. If the parameter is set to false, the return value is of the type string.

put.summary: Update the configuration of an identity provider.
put.description:
Update the configuration of an identity provider specified by the ID of the identity provider. The updates need to be provided in the JSON format. When you update an identity provider, certain limitations apply depending on what protocol you use.

- **OpenID Connect**
  - With OIDC as the default identity provider, the following properties can be changed:
    - `active` (only in feature set A)
    - `linkText`
    - `showLinkText`
    - `addShadowUserOnLogin`            
  - With OIDC as a custom identity provider, the following properties can be changed:
    - `active`
    - `linkText`
    - `showLinkText`
    - `addShadowUserOnLogin`            
    - `providerDescription`            
    - `iasTenant`, for example: `"iasTenant": { "host":"mytenant.accounts.ondemand.com", "deleteUsers":false, "refreshTrust":false}`. The property `iasTenant` is optional and will switch your existing trust configuration to another Identity Authentication tenant. Additionally, the optional `deleteUsers` property controls whether to delete all existing shadow users of the trust configuration. Use false (default value) when the new Identity Authentication tenant provides the same set of users, with the same user names. This ensures that users keep their authorizations, and application data associated with the users remains in place. Use true if the new Identity Authentication tenant provides a different set of users or different user names. Finally, the optional `refreshTrush` property enables you to get the current tenant information from Identity Authentication, for example, if the issuer changed. Use true to update the data SAP Authentication and Trust Management service stores locally about the Identity Authentication tenant. The default value of `refreshTrust` is false.
- **LDAP**
Only the property `active`can be changed.
- **SAML**
No limitations apply.

delete.summary: Delete an identity provider from your subaccount.
delete.description:
Delete an identity provider specified from your subaccount. The identity provider is specified by the ID of the identity provider. When you delete an identity provider, certain limitations apply depending on what protocol you use.

- **OpenID Connect**
If you have a subaccount based on the feature set B, you can't delete the default OIDC identity provider. A custom OIDC identity provider that exists next to the default can be deleted.
- **SAML**
No limitations apply.

put.summary: Migrate from SAML trust configuration to OpenID Connect Trust with Identity Authentication.
put.description: If your subaccount uses the SAML protocol to connect to your custom identity provider, you can't consume applications or application features that require direct authentication with Identity Authentication, such as SAP Build Work Zone and SAP Build Apps. To consume such applications or features, switch to using OpenID Connect (OIDC) with Identity Authentication. For an detailed view of the migration process, including preparation and testing, see [Migration from SAML Trust to OpenID Connect Trust with Identity Authentication](https://help.sap.com/docs/BTP/65de2977205c403bbc107264b8eccf4b/d097ce26cb2d4b8fa9a597a5381cb3cb.html) on the SAP Help Portal.

get.summary: Returns a list of available Identity Authentication tenants.
get.description: Returns an array of the tenants of SAP Cloud Identity Services - Identity Authentication available for trust configuration with your current SAP BTP account. Available tenants are associated with the same customer ID as your SAP BTP global account. Some Identity Authentication tenants have multiple customer IDs associated with them. The method returns all tenants by default. To return only those tenants which have the same customer ID as their primary ID, use the query parameter all=false.

parameters.name: all
parameters.description: Return all tenants with the same customer ID, irregardless of whether the ID is primary or secondary.

200.description: OK - Returns an array of Identity Authentication tenants.

For more information, see [Configure the Subject Name Identifier Sent to the Application](https://help.sap.com/docs/cloud-identity-services/cloud-identity-services/configure-subject-name-identifier-sent-to-application?version=Cloud). For PUT requests you can only set this value if you change to a different tenant.
